title: Doubloon SDK fails to load sprites

posts.cooked:
Hey everyone, I just started playing around with the Doubloon SDK for the remaster project and hit a snag when trying to load sprites in the compass-editor. No matter what I try, the sprites just won’t appear in the preview or the final build. I’m running a modded version of the SDK too, so I’m wondering if that’s causing some conflicts.

Has anyone else experienced this? I’ve double-checked the sprite file paths and formats, and everything seems to follow the guidelines exactly. The editor even gives a warning about missing texture references, but the files are definitely there. I feel like the engine might be bugging out on sprite loading specifically in modded environments.

Would love to hear if there’s a workaround or a fix in a future patch. If anyone has some deep-dive debug tips or similar experiences, please share! It’s a killer feature for the remaster, so getting sprites to show up properly would be a huge help.

posts.cooked:
Hey, I ran into the same issue with the Doubloon SDK where the sprites just don’t load in the compass-editor after applying some mods. From what I gathered digging through the logs, it looks like the remaster’s updated asset pipeline changed the way sprites need to be referenced, so older mod configurations or even some community-made ones hit a dead-end.

A quick workaround I found was to double-check that all sprite files are not only in the correct folder structure but also explicitly listed in the new asset manifest the remaster uses. If they’re missing from there, the editor seems to silently fail to load them, which is super frustrating because it doesn’t throw a clear error. Rebuilding the manifest or running the “refresh assets” command manually tends to get things back on track temporarily.

I’m hoping the SDK team patches this soon because modders are really going to hit a wall if they have to rework everything from scratch or jump through hoops just to see their sprites. Meanwhile, if anyone’s found a more permanent or automated fix, I’m all ears!

Hey there! I ran into the same issue with the Doubloon SDK not loading sprites properly, especially when working in the Compass Editor with modded content. From what I’ve gathered, it seems related to how the SDK handles asset indexing after remaster updates. The sprites aren’t missing, but the SDK isn’t recognizing the file paths correctly, which causes them not to appear when you try loading them.

A workaround that helped me was manually re-linking the sprite assets in the Compass Editor by refreshing the asset cache. You can do this by hitting the “Reload Assets” option in the editor’s settings menu, which forces the SDK to rebuild its database. It’s not ideal, but it makes your modded sprites show up again without crashing or freezing. Also, double-check that your sprite files are named exactly as the SDK expects—sometimes even small mismatches cause it to hiccup.

Hopefully the maintainers patch this soon because it’s pretty annoying when remaster projects get stuck on something like this. If you find any better fixes or are able to figure out a cleaner way to get the sprites loading smoothly again, please share! It’d make everyone’s workflow a lot easier.

posts.cooked:
Hey, I ran into the same issue when trying to load sprites in the Doubloon SDK, especially with the latest remaster update. It seems like the compass-editor isn’t properly linking to the modded assets folder, so any custom sprites just refuse to show up. I double-checked my file paths and naming conventions, and everything matches the docs, but no luck.

One workaround I found was to manually place the sprite files into the base assets directory, but that kinda defeats the purpose of modding cleanly. Also, the console spits out some vague “sprite load failed” warnings without much detail, so debugging is a pain. I hope the devs patch this soon because it’s a major blocker for anyone trying to customize their maps.

If anyone has found a more reliable fix or a hidden config tweak, I’d love to hear it. Otherwise, I guess we’re stuck waiting for the official update or risking messy file juggling. Fingers crossed they address this in the next patch!
